title: Self-hosted model evaluation capacity and observability
summary: Determine whether a self-hosted evaluation workload has enough capacity and whether the available evidence supports that conclusion. The procedure also separates deterministic citation checks from assessments of whether a citation supports a claim.
prerequisites: A representative evaluation workload and its expected outputs
Access to workload timing, completion, failure and resource-use records
Written acceptance criteria for evaluation quality and operating capacity

sections.title: Answer and update
paragraphs: For an intermediate practitioner asking whether evaluation capacity is sufficient, run a representative workload at controlled concurrency, record queueing, completion time, failures and resource use, and accept only the highest tested load that satisfies the written quality and operating criteria. If those measurements are unavailable or incomplete, capacity is not verified; restore evidence collection and repeat the run rather than inferring a result.

The previous source record had no reader-openable HTTPS URL and its verification date was unreliable. It has been replaced with the canonical HTTPS source listed at the end, and the item-level and source-level verification dates have been corrected. This source change affects the citation-grading guidance only: deterministic checks can establish citation presence, format or an exact expected value, but they do not generally establish whether cited material supports a claim. The capacity and observability procedure is otherwise unchanged.
sections.callout: Treat citation structure and citation support as separate evaluation questions.

sections.title: Capacity observation procedure
paragraphs: Step 1: Define the representative inputs, concurrency levels, quality criteria and operating limits before starting. If the workload or limits are missing, stop and obtain written criteria; proceeding without them cannot produce a defensible capacity result.

Step 2: Run the workload at a controlled starting level and retain start times, queue waits, completion times, outcomes, failures and corresponding resource-use records. If a record cannot be associated with its run, repair the collection or correlation method and repeat that run.

Step 3: Increase concurrency one tested level at a time while applying the same criteria. If a level exceeds an operating limit, produces unacceptable failures or misses the quality criteria, return to the last passing level, preserve the failed-run evidence and investigate the recorded constraint before testing again.

Step 4: Use deterministic grading only for properties it can directly decide, such as whether a citation is present, follows the required structure or exactly matches an expected value. When the question is whether the cited material supports a claim, use a documented semantic assessment or human review. If reviewers or assessment methods disagree, mark the item unresolved, adjudicate a sample against the written rubric and revise the rubric before rerunning affected items.

sections.title: Expected evidence and verification
paragraphs: Expected evidence consists of the workload definition, acceptance criteria, results for each tested concurrency level, timestamped operating measurements, failure records and the grading rubric. The evidence should identify the highest tested level that passed every stated criterion and the first tested level that did not, when a failing level was reached.

Verify the result by tracing each capacity conclusion to the retained run records and by confirming that every passing claim satisfies the written criteria. If a conclusion lacks a traceable record, classify it as unverified, restore or recollect the missing evidence and repeat the affected run.

Verify citation grading separately by inspecting examples from each grading path. Deterministic results should demonstrate only presence, structure or exact matching; support judgments should include the claim, cited material and recorded rationale. If a support judgment contains only a format result, withdraw that judgment and send the item through the documented semantic or human review path.
